segments.he: ענין שלש תפלות ביום. דהינו שתים ביום ואחד בלילה זה בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי לשון תרגום. שהיא בחינת שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום. כמבאר במאמר 'תפלה לחבקוק' לקוטי חלק א סימן יט. כי התפלה היא בחינת מלכות כמובא , בחינת חוה אשה. בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש ועל כן מתפללין שתי תפלות ביום ואחד בלילה. בבחינת שנים מקרא ואחד תרגום כנזכר לעיל. כי שנים מקרא זה בחינת תורה שבכתב שהיא בחינת יום כמובא בדברי רבנו זכרונו לברכה (שם סימן ג). וכנגד זה מתפללין שתי תפלות ביום, ואחד תרגום זה בחינת לילה שהוא בחינת שנה תרדמה, בחינת תרגום. כמבאר היטב במאמר הנזכר לעיל. והיא בחינת תורה שבעל פה. כי התרגום הוא פרוש התורה, והוא בכלל תורה שבעל פה. גם רב תורה שבעל פה דהינו התלמוד נתקן בלשון תרגום. כי תרגום הוא בחינת תורה שבעל פה שהיא בחינת לילה כמו שכתב רבנו זכרונו לברכה ועל כן מתפללין תפלה אחת בלילה, כנגד בחינת אחד תרגום שהוא בחינת לילה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן יעקב תקן תפלת ערבית. כי עקר בנין בחינת חוה אשה, הוא על ידי תרדמה. הינו עקר בנין ושלמות לשון הקדש הוא דיקא על ידי לשון תרגום כמו שמבאר שם. ויעקב זכה לזה דהינו שזכה לשלמות לשון הקדש על ידי התרגום. דהינו על ידי שנלחם והכניע אחיזת הרע שבתרגום. שהוא בחינת עץ הדעת טוב ורע וברר הטוב משם. ועל ידי זה זכה לשלמות לשון הקדש. ועל כן יעקב בחיר שבאבות ומטתו שלמה בלי שום פסול . שזה בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש, שהוא בחינת מטה שלמה, בחינת שמירת הברית בשלמות שזוכין על ידי שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי התרגום כמבאר שם. וכמו שכתוב ביעקב שאמר כחי וראשית אוני. דהינו שמירת הברית שזוכין על ידי זה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן זכה להעמיד שנים עשר שבטים שהם בחינת שנים עשר בקר שמלכות דקדשה עומדת עליהם. הינו בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש בחינת שמירת הברית. וזה בחינת שבעים נפש שיצאו מיעקב . שזכה לזה על ידי בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש. שעל ידי זה מכניעין רע הכולל של שבעים אמין. ועל כן זכה להעמיד שבעים נפשות בית יעקב. וכל זה העקר על ידי לשון תרגום שהוא בחינת עץ הדעת. שיעקב היה עוסק לתקן ולברר העץ הדעת לתקן פגם אדם הראשון כמובא . כי השבעים נפשות בית יעקב ולהפך השבעים עממין כלם נאחזים בבחינת שרש אחיזת העץ הדעת ששם הוא בחינת יעקב כמובא בכתבים . ועל כן עקר מלחמות יעקב היה עם חותנו לבן הארמי. כי לבן הארמי הוא בחינת תרגום, שהוא לשון ארמי. וכמו שכתב רבנו זכרונו לברכה במאמר הנזכר לעיל. שלבן קרא לו יגר שהדותא, כדי להמשיך ולינק מן הקדשה על ידי לשון תרגום. ויעקב קרא לו גלעד כדי להשלים לשון הקדש עין שם:

עִנְיַן שָׁלֹשׁ תְּפִלּוֹת בַּיּוֹם דְּהַיְנוּ שְׁתַּיִם בַּיּוֹם וְאֶחָד בַּלַּיְלָה: 

זֶה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם כַּמְבֹאָר בַּמַּאֲמָר 'תְּפִלָּה לַחֲבַקּוּק' לִקּוּטֵי חֵלֶק א סִימָן יט: 

כִּי הַתְּפִלָּה הִיא בְּחִינַת מַלְכוּת כַּמּוּבָא, בְּחִינַת חַוָּה אִשָּׁה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ. וְעַל-כֵּן מִתְפַּלְּלִין שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת בַּיּוֹם וְאֶחָד בַּלַּיְלָה בִּבְחִינַת שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. כִּי שְׁנַיִם מִקְרָא זֶה בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת יוֹם כַּמּוּבָא בְּדִבְרֵי רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם סִימָן ג) וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה מִתְפַּלְּלִין שְׁתֵּי תְּפִלּוֹת בַּיּוֹם. וְאֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם זֶה בְּחִינַת לַיְלָה שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת שֵׁנָה תַּרְדֵּמָה, בְּחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם, כַּמְבֹאָר הֵיטֵב בַּמַּאֲמָר הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וְהִיא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה. כִּי הַתַּרְגּוּם הוּא פֵּרוּשׁ הַתּוֹרָה, וְהוּא בִּכְלַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה גַּם רֹב תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה דְּהַיְנוּ הַתַּלְמוּד נִתְקַן בִּלְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם כִּי תַּרְגּוּם הוּא בְּחִינַת תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת לַיְלָה כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה (שָׁם). וְעַל-כֵּן מִתְפַּלְּלִין תְּפִלָּה אַחַת בַּלַּיְלָה, כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת אֶחָד תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת לַיְלָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית. כִּי עִקַּר בִּנְיַן בְּחִינַת חַוָּה אִשָּׁה, הוּא עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְדֵּמָה הַיְנוּ עִקַּר בִּנְיַן וּשְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ הוּא דַּיְקָא עַל-יְדֵי לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם. וְיַעֲקֹב זָכָה לָזֶה דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי הַתַּרְגּוּם דְּהַיְנוּ עַל-יְדֵי שֶׁנִּלְחַם וְהִכְנִיעַ אֲחִיזַת הָרַע שֶׁבַּתַּרְגּוּם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע וּבֵרֵר הַטּוֹב מִשָּׁם וְעַל-יְדֵי זֶה זָכָה לִשְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ. וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב בָּחִיר שֶׁבָּאָבוֹת וּמִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה בְּלִי שׁוּם פְּסוּל. שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת מִטָּה שְׁלֵמָה, בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית בִּשְׁלֵמוּת שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל-יְדֵי שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי הַתַּרְגּוּם כַּמְבֹאָר שָׁם. וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּיַעֲקֹב שֶׁאָמַר כֹּחִי וְרֵאשִׁית אוֹנִי, דְּהַיְנוּ שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית שֶׁזּוֹכִין עַל-יְדֵי זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן זָכָה לְהַעֲמִיד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים שֶׁהֵם בְּחִינַת שְׁנַיִם עָשָׂר בָּקָר שֶׁמַּלְכוּת דִּקְדֻשָּׁה עוֹמֶדֶת עֲלֵיהֶם. הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית. וְזֶה בְּחִינַת שִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיָּצְאוּ מִיַּעֲקֹב, שֶׁזָּכָה לָזֶה עַל-יְדֵי בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ. שֶׁעַל-יְדֵי זֶה מַכְנִיעִין רַע הַכּוֹלֵל שֶׁל שִׁבְעִים אֻמִּין. וְעַל-כֵּן זָכָה לְהַעֲמִיד שִׁבְעִים נַפְשׁוֹת בֵּית יַעֲקֹב. וְכָל זֶה הָעִקָּר עַל-יְדֵי לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב הָיָה עוֹסֵק לְתַקֵּן וּלְבָרֵר הָעֵץ הַדַּעַת לְתַקֵּן פְּגַם אָדָם הָרִאשׁוֹן כַּמּוּבָא. כִּי הַשִּׁבְעִים נַפְשׁוֹת בֵּית יַעֲקֹב וּלְהֵפֶךְ הַשִּׁבְעִים עֲמָמִין כֻּלָּם נֶאֱחָזִים בִּבְחִינַת שֹׁרֶשׁ אֲחִיזַת הָעֵץ הַדַּעַת שֶׁשָּׁם הוּא בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב כַּמּוּבָא בַּכְּתָבִים. וְעַל-כֵּן עִקַּר מִלְחֲמוֹת יַעֲקֹב הָיָה עִם חוֹתְנוֹ לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי. כִּי לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי הוּא בְּחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן אֲרַמִּי וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב רַבֵּנוּ זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה בַּמַּאֲמָר הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל שֶׁלָּבָן קָרָא לוֹ יְגַר שָׂהֲדוּתָא, כְּדֵי לְהַמְשִׁיךְ וְלִינֹק מִן הַקְּדֻשָּׁה עַל-יְדֵי לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם. וְיַעֲקֹב קָרָא לוֹ "גַּלְעֵד" כְּדֵי לְהַשְׁלִים לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַיֵּן שָׁם:

את נשיו מבנות לבן דיקא. הינו שזכה לבחינת חוה אשה שהיא בחינת לאה ורחל, על ידי תרגום שהוא בחינת לבן כנזכר לעיל. דהינו שהכניע הרע והוציא הטוב, שעל ידי זה דיקא נבנה בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש, בחינת חוה אשה בחינת לאה ורחל. ועל כן זכה יעקב לתכלית השלמות והיתה מטתו שלמה, והעמיד שנים עשר שבטים ושבעים נפש. כי זכה להכניע הרע שבתרגום ולברר הטוב, עד שזכה לבחינת שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי תרגום דיקא. דהינו שזכה לקח לאה ורחל מבית לבן דיקא, שהוא בחינת תרגום כנזכר לעיל. וזה ששלח יעקב לעשו עם לבן גרתי וכו'. כי יעקב ברח מעשו ללבן, דהינו שיעקב היה יודע שאי אפשר להכניע את עשו שהוא זהמת הנחש רע הכולל, כי אם על ידי שיבטל יניקתו, דהינו שיכניע הרע שבתרגום שמשם הם יונקים ויעלה הטוב ללשון הקדש. ואזי עשו שהוא בחינת רע הכולל ממילא יהיה נופל ונתבטל כמו שמבאר שם במאמר הנזכר לעיל. ועל כן ברח יעקב ללבן דיקא כדי לתקן לשון תרגום ואזי יפל עשו ממילא כנזכר לעיל. וזכה לנצח אותו והוציא משם דיקא בחינת לשון הקדש, דהינו חוה אשה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן אמר אעבדך שבע שנים, כנגד בחינת השבעים עממין שכלולים בשבע, שיניקתם מבחינת לבן מבחינת תרגום כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן הצרך לעבד לו דיקא אותן השבע שנים. כי כשרוצין לברר הטוב מתוך הרע צריכין לעבר שם ולסבל גלות ועבדות שלהם, ולעמד בנסיון לשברם ולהכניעם, ואזי דיקא מבררין הטוב משם. ועל כן אחר גלות השבע שנים שזה בחינת גלות שבעים עממין כנזכר לעיל, אז זכה לבחינת שלמות לשון הקדש שהיא בחינת רחל ולאה כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן היה מצפה עד שנולד יוסף שהוא בחינת תקון הברית. ואז כאשר ילדה רחל את יוסף, אז נתחזק דעתו והבין שזכה לשלמות לשון הקדש על ידי תרגום, עד שזכה על ידי זה ליוסף דהינו שמירת הברית. ועל כן אמר אז שלחני וכו'. ואמרו רבותינו זכרונם לברכה שלא היה מתירא עוד מעשו מאחר שנולד יוסף שהוא שטנו וכו'. הינו כי בודאי אין לו להתירא עתה מאחר שזכה להעמיד את יוסף על ידי רחל בת לבן הארמי. שזה בחינת שמירת הברית על ידי שזוכין ללשון הקדש שבונין אותו על ידי תרגום דיקא כנזכר לעיל. וזה שכתוב 'כאשר ילדה רחל את יוסף', רחל דיקא. שהיא בחינת לשון הקדש והיא בת לבן. כי בנינה מתרגום כנזכר לעיל. ועל ידי זה דיקא נולד יוסף בחינת שמירת הברית כנזכר לעיל. כי שמירת הברית זוכין על ידי שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי תרגום, כמו שמבאר היטב במאמר הנזכר לעיל עין שם. ואז בודאי לא נתירא עוד מעשו שהוא רע הכולל, כי הוא נופל ממילא, בבחינת לשון נופל על לשון, כמו שמבאר שם עין שם. ועל כן תחלת דברי יעקב ששלח לעשו הוא עם לבן גרתי, עם לבן דיקא, שהוא לשון תרגום. שהכניע הרע משם וברר הטוב. ואזי עשו נופל ממילא כנזכר לעיל. וזהו ויהי לי שור וחמור צאן וכו'. הינו בחינת ניצוצות טובות ועשירות שברר משם. ועל כן הלך עשו אל ישמעאל. כי הכל הולך למינו. הינו כי איתא שעשו וישמעאל הם כלליות השבעים אמין. ועל כן הלך לשם כדי שיתחברו יחד הרע של כלליות השבעים אמין, כדי להתגבר על יעקב חס ושלום. אבל יעקב על ידי שהכניע את לבן היה מתגבר עליהם כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
"Yaakov lived in the land of Egypt seventeen years." It is explained in our Sages' words (Midrash Rabbah) and especially in the holy Zohar on this parshah that those seventeen years were the essential years of his life — he lived in joy and contentment, as stated there in the holy Zohar. At first glance this is astonishing: when he dwelt in Eretz Yisrael he had no peace, yet in impure Egypt — where the Egyptian exile began and they embittered their lives — specifically there he dwelt in peace!

But all this is the aspect of "gladness and joy shall they attain" etc. The essential completeness of joy in Him (= the essential vitality) is when one overpowers to seize sorrow and sighing and transform it to joy — the essential sorting from the Chambers of Exchange, accomplished through joy, essentially through exchanging and transforming sorrow and sighing to joy. The totality of all the forefathers' service was to reveal and make known His G-dliness in the world — the sole purpose of man's existence, and all his joy and vitality. For it is known to all that this world is full of anger, anguish, sorrow, and sighing, ending in death, and the days of our lives are vanity, etc. There is no joy or vitality in the world except through the sparkling of truth and emunah. "Truth is the elixir of life," as our Sages say. The essential truth is Hashem: "the truth of Hashem is forever." To believe in the truth of His existence and to strive and labor all one's days to draw close and cling to Him: "to Him you shall cling" — this is all vitality: "choose life, so that you and your seed may live — to love Hashem your G-d and to cling to Him, for He is your life."

But this clinging in completeness is impossible unless one shatters all bodily desires completely — like the forefathers, who merited drawing holy emunah upon themselves each time until they came to great joy through this. Through this they sorted each time from the Chambers of Exchange, ascending through all the above ascents, perceiving the Ain Sof light in mati v'lo mati — each according to his level, for there are many levels in this. The entire order of every Jew's daily service — especially the order of tefilah with tallis and tefillin, etc. — is all the aspect of the above ascents explained in the Torah "Amtza'isa": raising Malchus from the klipos, Netzach-Hod-Yesod clothing Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes, and Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes clothing Chochmah-Binah-Da'as, etc. — from world to world; see the kavanos and the above Torah well, and a little will sparkle for you.

Although the forefathers and great tzadikim shattered the body completely, meriting the essential completeness of this joy in Him ("rejoice, tzadikim, in Hashem"; "the righteous shall rejoice and exult before G-d and be glad with joy") — their entire labor was to rectify all the world, to draw this holy joy and vitality into the heart of every Jew. Even one who has not completely shattered his bodily desires can also draw close to Hashem through guarding the Torah and mitzvos. Even one who has flawed as he has flawed — whenever he desires and strives to draw close to Hashem, he can gladden and revive his soul through the great power of the tzadikim: by believing that every single good point merited through every mitzvah he performs is beyond measure. Even the good points of the mitzvos performed by the sinners of Israel surpass all the pleasures, wealth, etc. of the entire world — until they greatly gladden their souls that they too merit such true, eternal good: engaging in mitzvos, through which they cling to Hashem, the Life of all lives, the Source of the joy of all joys. As it says: "I shall come to the G-d of my joyful exultation"; "You shall make known to me the path of life; fullness of joys is Your countenance" — all the aspect of "gladness and joy shall they attain": seizing sorrow and sighing and transforming it to joy.

This is the aspect of all the exiles Israel undergoes — whose essence is the exile of the soul, far from its Father in Heaven, whose essential exile is sadness, as above. Due to the sin of Adam HaRishon and the corruptions of each generation, one must be in exile — until, through the power of the great tzadikim, the sorting from the Chambers of Exchange is accomplished specifically through this. The essential sorting is through joy — transforming sorrow and sighing to joy. This is the aspect of Yosef's sale to Egypt, through which specifically they could survive in Egypt: "G-d sent me before you for sustenance." Yosef is the inflaming of joy through the above aspect, as above. Even Yaakov our father and his holy sons — the totality of Israel's holiness — were compelled to descend to Egypt, and specifically there Yaakov lived in joy and contentment. For then he perceived in completeness that the final ge'ulah would come specifically through this: the tzadikim descending into the very depths of the Chambers of Exchange (= Egypt and all the exiles named after Egypt, as is known), sorting the holiness from there specifically — all through transforming sorrow and sighing to joy: the essential sorting from the Chambers of Exchange. The Chambers of Exchange want the opposite — to exchange and reverse everything, chas v'shalom — their reversed reasoning beyond telling, without end. But the single point of the great true tzadikim surpasses everything — they exchange and reverse for good, transforming sorrow and sighing to joy, as above.

§ 52 — Yaakov's Burial in Eretz Yisrael: The Lights of the Tzachtzachos and the Resurrection

Therefore Yaakov made Yosef swear to bury him in Eretz Yisrael. There is the essential holy Place deriving from the above supernal Place (= the Arranger, called Place), from which the above nine chambers are perceived — the lights of the tzachtzachos [brilliant splendors]. This is the essential perception of the tzadikim, merited in completeness after their passing: "He shall satisfy your soul with tzachtzachos" etc. Death was decreed because Adam HaRishon flawed the Arranger and Settler, as above — for which death was decreed for all generations. Now it is impossible for anyone, even the most complete tzadikim, to attain the lights of the tzachtzachos in their lifetime in completeness; each according to his service perceives what he perceives in this lifetime. Ultimately one must die and return to the dust: "to dust you shall return."

There specifically, the body will decompose, be purified, and be transformed to holy dust — the aspect of holy ground (= the above awesome Place). This is the transformation from sadness, sorrow, and sighing to vitality and joy — through which one will rise at the Resurrection of the Dead, when the essential joy will be in completeness: "then our mouths will be filled with laughter"; "in the future, Hashem will make a dance for the righteous, each one pointing with his finger" etc. — "we shall exult and rejoice in His salvation." Fortunate is one who merits burial in Eretz Yisrael, where the holy Place resides — through which one is encompassed in the above Place ("blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place"), perceiving the lights of the tzachtzachos (= the nine chambers). Fortunate is one who merits this.

§ 53 — Yaakov Sought to Reveal the End — and Was Obstructed

"Yaakov called to his sons" etc. — he sought to reveal the end of the ge'ulah, but the Shechinah departed from him. The essential ge'ulah is through joy: "for with joy you shall go out." At first Yaakov thought the sorting from the Chambers of Exchange was already complete enough to reveal the end. But the Shechinah departed — the aspect of "into what is wondrous for you, do not seek": from the obstructer, which strikes the pursuing mind and does not allow it to pursue excessively, especially regarding the end of the ge'ulah — the wondrous end ("the heart does not reveal to the mouth").

Therefore he began speaking of other matters: "gather together" etc. — the essential tikun through the gathering of Israel, the aspect of peace: gathering and listening to Yaakov and Yisrael (= the true tzadikim). Through this, the complete ge'ulah will ultimately come through their awesome power — through transforming sorrow and sighing to joy, as above.

§ 54 — Yaakov's Rebuke of the Three Tribes: The Flaw of the Arranger and Settler

Yaakov rebuked the first three tribes — his essential rebuke was that they flawed the tikun of the Arranger and Settler, from which the errors and mistakes of even great tzadikim derive, as above.

"Reuven, you are my firstborn, my strength, the beginning of my vigor" — the tikun of the bris, as our Sages expound. There is the essential joy: "strength and gladness are in His place" — the opposite of the flaw of the bris (= wailing and sadness). Since he was born in such holiness, he deserved "extra dignity and extra strength" (= priesthood and kingship, the above tikunim). Through joy Malchus is raised — the aspect of oz [strength]: "Hashem — in Your strength the king rejoices"; and all the above blessings — "extra dignity": "Aharon raised his hands to the people and blessed them."

נִמְצָא שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב שֶׁעִקָּרוֹ לְתַקֵּן הָעֵץ הַדַּעַת, עַל-כֵּן הָיָה עוֹסֵק לְהַכְנִיעַ בְּחִינַת לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי, הַיְנוּ לְהַכְנִיעַ הָרַע שֶׁבַּתַּרְגּוּם וּלְהַעֲלוֹת הַטּוֹב לִבְנוֹת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, בְּחִינַת חַוָּה אִשָּׁה עַל-יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן לָקַח יַעֲקֹב אֶת נָשָׁיו מִבְּנוֹת לָבָן דַּיְקָא. הַיְנוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְחִינַת חַוָּה אִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת לֵאָה וְרָחֵל, עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת לָבָן כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁהִכְנִיעַ הָרַע וְהוֹצִיא הַטּוֹב, שֶׁעַל-יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא נִבְנָה בְּחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, בְּחִינַת חַוָּה אִשָּׁה בְּחִינַת לֵאָה וְרָחֵל. וְעַל-כֵּן זָכָה יַעֲקֹב לְתַכְלִית הַשְּׁלֵמוּת וְהָיְתָה מִטָּתוֹ שְׁלֵמָה, וְהֶעֱמִיד שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר שְׁבָטִים וְשִׁבְעִים נֶפֶשׁ. כִּי זָכָה לְהַכְנִיעַ הָרַע שֶׁבַּתַּרְגּוּם וּלְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב, עַד שֶׁזָּכָה לִבְחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְגּוּם דַּיְקָא דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁזָּכָה לִקַּח לֵאָה וְרָחֵל מִבֵּית לָבָן דַּיְקָא, שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. 

וְזֶה שֶׁשָּׁלַח יַעֲקֹב לְעֵשָׂו "עִם לָבָן גַּרְתִּי וְכוּ'" כִּי יַעֲקֹב בָּרַח מֵעֵשָׂו לְלָבָן, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּעֲקֹב הָיָה יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לְהַכְנִיעַ אֶת עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא זֻהֲמַת הַנָּחָשׁ רַע הַכּוֹלֵל, כִּי אִם עַל-יְדֵי שֶׁיְּבַטֵּל יְנִיקָתוֹ, דְּהַיְנוּ שֶׁיַּכְנִיעַ הָרַע שֶׁבַּתַּרְגּוּם שֶׁמִּשָּׁם הֵם יוֹנְקִים וְיַעֲלֶה הַטּוֹב לִלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ. וַאֲזַי עֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת רַע הַכּוֹלֵל מִמֵּילָא יִהְיֶה נוֹפֵל וְנִתְבַּטֵּל כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם בַּמַּאֲמָר הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן בָּרַח יַעֲקֹב לְלָבָן דַּיְקָא כְּדֵי לְתַקֵּן לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם וַאֲזַי יִפֹּל עֵשָׂו מִמֵּילָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְזָכָה לְנַצֵּחַ אוֹתוֹ וְהוֹצִיא מִשָּׁם דַּיְקָא בְּחִינַת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ, דְּהַיְנוּ חַוָּה אִשָּׁה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן אָמַר "אֶעֱבָדְךָ שֶׁבַע שָׁנִים", כְּנֶגֶד בְּחִינַת הַשִּׁבְעִים עֲמָמִין שֶׁכְּלוּלִים בְּשֶׁבַע, שֶׁיְּנִיקָתָם מִבְּחִינַת לָבָן מִבְּחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. 

וְעַל-כֵּן הֻצְרַךְ לַעֲבֹד לוֹ דַּיְקָא אוֹתָן הַשֶּׁבַע שָׁנִים. כִּי כְּשֶׁרוֹצִין לְבָרֵר הַטּוֹב מִתּוֹךְ הָרַע צְרִיכִין לַעֲבֹר שָׁם וְלִסְבֹּל גָּלוּת וְעַבְדוּת שֶׁלָּהֶם, וְלַעֲמֹד בְּנִסָּיוֹן לְשַׁבְּרָם וּלְהַכְנִיעָם, וַאֲזַי דַּיְקָא מְבָרְרִין הַטּוֹב מִשָּׁם. וְעַל-כֵּן אַחַר גָּלוּת הַשֶּׁבַע שָׁנִים שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת גָּלוּת שִׁבְעִים עֲמָמִין כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל, אָז זָכָה לִבְחִינַת שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת רָחֵל וְלֵאָה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן הָיָה מְצַפֶּה עַד שֶׁנּוֹלַד יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּן הַבְּרִית. וְאָז כַּאֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה רָחֵל אֶת יוֹסֵף, אָז נִתְחַזֵּק דַּעְתּוֹ וְהֵבִין שֶׁזָּכָה לִשְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְגּוּם, עַד שֶׁזָּכָה עַל-יְדֵי זֶה לְיוֹסֵף דְּהַיְנוּ שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית. וְעַל-כֵּן אָמַר אָז "שַׁלְּחֵנִי וְכוּ'", וְאָמְרוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה מִתְיָרֵא עוֹד מֵעֵשָׂו מֵאַחַר שֶׁנּוֹלַד יוֹסֵף שֶׁהוּא שְׂטָנוֹ וְכוּ'. הַיְנוּ כִּי בְּוַדַּאי אֵין לוֹ לְהִתְיָרֵא עַתָּה מֵאַחַר שֶׁזָּכָה לְהַעֲמִיד אֶת יוֹסֵף עַל-יְדֵי רָחֵל בַּת לָבָן הָאֲרַמִּי. שֶׁזֶּה בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית עַל-יְדֵי שֶׁזּוֹכִין לִלְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ שֶׁבּוֹנִין אוֹתוֹ עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְגּוּם דַּיְקָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְזֶה שֶׁכָּתוּב 'כַּאֲשֶׁר יָלְדָה רָחֵל אֶת יוֹסֵף', "רָחֵל" דַּיְקָא שֶׁהִיא בְּחִינַת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְהִיא בַּת לָבָן. כִּי בִּנְיָנָהּ מִתַּרְגּוּם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-יְדֵי זֶה דַּיְקָא נוֹלַד יוֹסֵף בְּחִינַת שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. כִּי שְׁמִירַת הַבְּרִית זוֹכִין עַל-יְדֵי שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי תַּרְגּוּם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר הֵיטֵב בַּמַּאֲמָר הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל עַיֵּן שָׁם, וְאָז בְּוַדַּאי לֹא נִתְיָרֵא עוֹד מֵעֵשָׂו שֶׁהוּא רַע הַכּוֹלֵל, כִּי הוּא נוֹפֵל מִמֵּילָא, בִּבְחִינַת לָשׁוֹן נוֹפֵל עַל לָשׁוֹן, כְּמוֹ שֶׁמְּבֹאָר שָׁם עַיֵּן שָׁם. וְעַל-כֵּן תְּחִלַּת דִּבְרֵי יַעֲקֹב שֶׁשָּׁלַח לְעֵשָׂו הוּא עִם לָבָן גַּרְתִּי, עִם לָבָן דַּיְקָא, שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן תַּרְגּוּם. שֶׁהִכְנִיעַ הָרַע מִשָּׁם וּבֵרֵר הַטּוֹב. וַאֲזַי עֵשָׂו נוֹפֵל מִמֵּילָא כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְזֶהוּ "וַיְהִי לִי שׁוֹר וַחֲמוֹר צֹאן וְכוּ'" הַיְנוּ בְּחִינַת נִיצוֹצוֹת טוֹבוֹת וַעֲשִׁירוּת שֶׁבֵּרֵר מִשָּׁם. וְעַל-כֵּן הָלַךְ עֵשָׂו אֶל יִשְׁמָעֵאל כִּי הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ לְמִינוֹ הַיְנוּ כִּי אִיתָא שֶׁעֵשָׂו וְיִשְׁמָעֵאל הֵם כְּלָלִיּוּת הַשִּׁבְעִים אֻמִּין. וְעַל-כֵּן הָלַךְ לְשָׁם כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּתְחַבְּרוּ יַחַד הָרַע שֶׁל כְּלָלִיּוּת הַשִּׁבְעִים אֻמִּין, כְּדֵי לְהִתְגַּבֵּר עַל יַעֲקֹב חַס וְשָׁלוֹם. אֲבָל יַעֲקֹב עַל-יְדֵי שֶׁהִכְנִיעַ אֶת לָבָן הָיָה מִתְגַּבֵּר עֲלֵיהֶם כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:

segments.he: ועל-כן יעקב דיקא תקן תפלת ערבית. כי תפלת ערבית היא בחינת תרגום שעקר שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי זה כנזכר לעיל. וזה היה בחינת תקוני יעקב כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן ערבית מרמז בע' רבתי של שמ'ע', שהוא ראשי תבות שחרית מנחה ערבית כמו שאיתא בזהר הקדוש . כי ערבית היא בבחינת תרגום בבחינת עץ הדעת שמשם זוכין להכניע השבעים עממין ולזכות לבחינת שבעים נפשות בית יעקב כנזכר לעיל. והוא כנגד סכות שהוא בחינת יעקב. כי בסכות מכניעין השבעים אמין שמתמעטין והולכין כפרי החג:
segments.en:
"But reckless as water — you shall not excel": he rushed to show his anger — the above flaw. His mind pursued excessively until he came to anger — seeking to overturn the holy knowledge of Yaakov our father who placed his bed in Bilhah's tent. This is the flaw of the mind pursuing excessively through the flaw of the Arranger and Settler. "For then you desecrated my couch; he went up" — the perception of the Ain Sof light that Yaakov merited on his couch in awesome holiness, through properly rectifying the Arranger and Settler, through sorting joy from the Chambers of Exchange (the secret of why he had to raise holy tribes also from the handmaids). The essential above perceptions are merited by the tzadikim through the holiness of their union in ultimate holiness (as explained in Hilchos Periyah v'Riviyah 4 and in this Torah "Amtza'isa"; see there well). Reuven flawed greatly in this — seeking to outthink Yaakov's da'as, thereby flawing the Arranger and Settler — and therefore lost the priesthood and kingship (= the above tikunim, through which the Arranger is essentially rectified).

Likewise: "Shimon and Levi are brothers; instruments of violence are their wares." When one tries to seize knowledge and perceptions one is unworthy of — this is the aspect of theft, robbery, and anger. "Let my soul not enter their counsel" — "their secret [sodam]" specifically: it seemed to them they had already attained all the secrets and perceptions, until they insisted on selling Yosef the tzadik — seeming to them, according to their knowledge, that he strayed from the path of truth. Yaakov said: "let my soul not enter their counsel" — I do not want such secrets. "And in their assembly — of Korach and Zimri — let my honor not be joined" — they flawed even more greatly, drawn after their desires. Zimri wanted to commit adultery and argued with Moshe like a supposed scholar: "if you say this one is forbidden..." etc. Any person of true understanding knows the difference between Moshe Rabbainu's intent and Zimri's — Moshe was a great ascetic who married Yisro's daughter by Divine command, while Zimri followed his desire and brazenly wanted to permit public immorality. Korach desired personal honor, posing as an advocate for Israel: "the entire congregation is holy, and Hashem is in their midst — why do you exalt yourselves?"

All this derives from the flaw of the Arranger and Settler of the mind. Even great tzadikim like Shimon and Levi flawed in this subtly — not from desire, chas v'shalom, but from excessive inflaming for Hashem (= the flaw of the Arranger and Settler) — therefore they erred regarding Yosef. But Zimri and Korach flawed in this grossly — flawing the Settler until they lost all shame, brazening their faces as above.

Therefore Yaakov pleaded: "in their assembly let my honor not be joined" — "my honor" specifically. Yaakov is the root of Israel's holiness — their essential honor of Hashem through the service of tefilah with songs and praises, raising His honor through the joy of the mitzvah, meriting the tikun of the pursuit and obstructer properly: "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place," as explained in the above Torah — the ultimate completeness of unification. All unifications derive from there: when the pursuit is encompassed in the obstructer in mati v'lo mati properly, thereby begetting perceptions of G-dliness properly. Therefore Yaakov said: "let my honor not be joined" specifically — through their assembly, my honor will not be unified where it must be unified ("blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place"). This unification is accomplished only through the great tzadikim and through the holy gathering attached to them who nullify their minds before them — not through those who dispute Moshe and Aharon (= the true tzadikim). Korach and Zimri greatly flawed the Arranger and Settler, from which all holy unifications derive.

"Yehudah — your brothers shall thank you" — from him emerged David and Mashiach, who will merit this in completeness, rectifying everything speedily in our days, amain. David made himself all his days like a poor and destitute man: "I am a worm and not a man"; "Hashem, my heart is not haughty, my eyes not lofty; I did not walk in great matters and wonders beyond me" — concluding: "let Israel hope in Hashem from now and forever." The essential thing: to make oneself like a nursing child, etc. — and hope for Hashem's salvation, increasing songs, praises, prayers, and thanksgivings. Like David, who engaged in this all his days until he merited composing Sefer Tehillim, encompassing all ten types of melody (= the totality of joy in Him). This is the essential tikun through which the complete ge'ulah will come — through Mashiach from his seed, whose ge'ulah is through joy. Therefore he labored greatly to find the place of the Bais HaMikdash, where the light of holy joy is received: "I shall rejoice in Hashem"; "in Him our hearts rejoice."

§ 55 — The Twelve Tribes = The Twelve Months: Repairing the Moon's Blemish

This is the aspect of the twelve holy tribes Yaakov begot — the totality of Israel's holiness, the totality of joy in Him. They are twelve corresponding to the twelve months, as is known — for the twelve months are the tikun of the moon's blemish, the tikun of "luminaries" [spelled deficiently]. This is accomplished through the holy joy, as above.

§ 56 — The Birth of Each Tribe = A Tikun of Holy Joy

Each tribe's birth was in awesome holiness — the aspect of holy joy, the essential tikun of the bris, the essential tikun of the holy union (as explained in Hilchos Periyah v'Riviyah). Therefore all their holy names were called after the above tikunim accomplished through performing the mitzvah with joy.

Reuven — named for "see the difference between my son and my father-in-law's son" (= Esav, from whom all exiles come through sadness: "when you shall have cause to grieve," as above, ois yud-ches). Esav sold the birthright to Yaakov (= the holy joy of the sacrificial service — he had no desire for blessing, and it was distant from him). Afterward he grew jealous and pursued — the aspect of all exiles. Reuven is the opposite: he did not sell the birthright to Yosef; nevertheless he saved him — yielding his honor and nullifying himself before Yosef the tzadik (= the essential joy of Israel). Therefore Reuven is the aspect of sorting from the Chambers of Exchange: "see the difference between my son and my father-in-law's son" — Reuven's holiness (the firstborn of Israel's seed) was sorted from the klipah of Esav, through the joy with which he was born from Yaakov in such holiness (for he was the beginning of his vigor — the essential holiness of begetting is through joy). Therefore Reuven was the first to begin teshuvah, as the Midrash states (Beraishis Rabbah 84) — from him Hoshayah the prophet emerged. The essential teshuvah is sorting from the Chambers of Exchange, transforming sins to merits — transforming sorrow and sighing to joy (as explained in Hilchos Periyah v'Riviyah).

Shimon — the aspect of the worthy rebuker: "Hashem heard that I am hated." The rebuker is hated (as explained in the Torah "V'Aileh HaMishpatim," LM I:10). This is the aspect of the mitzvah going forth to arouse all to Hashem — the worthy rebuker who arouses the whole world to Hashem.

Levi — from him came the Kohanim, with whom all blessings reside: "Aharon raised his hands to the people and blessed them" — the tikun of the hands, Chesed-Gevurah-Tiferes, as explained there.

Yehudah — "this time I shall thank Hashem": the ultimate tikun of todah and thanksgiving, the essential completeness of joy through which one ascends to the Arranger. Then "she stopped bearing" — one must wait, as above. Even though more mental faculties (= holy offspring) must still be begotten, one cannot pursue excessively.

Then Rachel grew jealous of her sister: "give me children; if not, I am dead." She saw and understood that more holy offspring of Israel's seed were still needed (= the totality of joy in Him). She said: "if not, I am dead" — without children (= the essential joy), she is surely dead, for sadness is the side of death. "Yaakov's anger burned against Rachel: 'Am I in place of G-d?'" — it is impossible to force the time. She said: "here is my handmaid Bilhah" — she understood through ruach hakodesh that it was impossible to beget further holy offspring unless he descended again to the Chambers of Exchange and sorted the holiness from there. This parallels what Sarah our mother understood — Avraham could not beget Yitzchak without first marrying the handmaid Hagar. But from that union emerged Yishmael, from whom exile (= sadness) comes: "a foolish son is his mother's grief" — his mother was expelled because of him (Midrash). But Yaakov's bed was complete: he merited descending and ascending in ultimate completeness, raising holy tribes even from the handmaids (= joy) — sorting in completeness from the Chambers of Exchange that cling to the handmaids.
segments.he_nikud: וְעַל-כֵּן יַעֲקֹב דַּיְקָא תִּקֵּן תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית כִּי תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית הִיא בְּחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁעִקַּר שְׁלֵמוּת לְשׁוֹן הַקֹּדֶשׁ עַל-יְדֵי זֶה כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְזֶה הָיָה בְּחִינַת תִּקּוּנֵי יַעֲקֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל. וְעַל-כֵּן עַרְבִית מְרֻמָּז בְּע' רַבָּתִי שֶׁל שְׁמַ'ע', שֶׁהוּא רָאשֵׁי תֵּבוֹת שַׁחֲרִית מִנְחָה עַרְבִית כְּמוֹ שֶׁאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ. כִּי עַרְבִית הִיא בִּבְחִינַת תַּרְגּוּם בִּבְחִינַת עֵץ הַדַּעַת שֶׁמִּשָּׁם זוֹכִין לְהַכְנִיעַ הַשִּׁבְעִים עֲמָמִין וְלִזְכּוֹת לִבְחִינַת שִׁבְעִים נַפְשׁוֹת בֵּית יַעֲקֹב כַּנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל וְהוּא כְּנֶגֶד סֻכּוֹת שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת יַעֲקֹב כִּי בְּסֻכּוֹת מַכְנִיעִין הַשִּׁבְעִים אֻמִּין שֶׁמִּתְמַעֲטִין וְהוֹלְכִין כְּפָרֵי הֶחָג:

segments.he: וזהו בחינת תפלת ערבית רשות. כי תרגום הוא בחינת רשות בחינת התר שהוא בבחינת עץ הדעת נגה בחינת תרגום כמובא . כי חיוב מצוה ואסור הם בבחינת קדש והפוכו. אבל ההתר ורשות הם בבחינת תרגום עץ הדעת כמובא . ועל כן תפלת ערבית רשות כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
When Bilhah her handmaid bore a son, she named him Dan: "G-d has judged me and also heard my voice." She boasted that a holy son was sorted from the severity of judgment — sadness (= the severity of judgment) transformed to such joy that a holy tribe was born. Each of the tribes is the aspect of "a wise son gladdens a father." This was through her many prayers ("also heard my voice"). Through this, Malchus was sorted from the klipos — the aspect of Dan: "the law of the kingdom is law," as explained elsewhere.

Naftali — the tikun of the feet: "Naftali is a hind let loose"; "in the valley, he sent forth his feet" (Shoftim 5).

Gad — the tikun of the hands: "he tears the arm and also the skull" of the Sitra Achra. Through him the hands were rectified — through which the blessing of intellect is received (= the head and skull): "raise your hands in holiness"; "Aharon raised his hands" — they must be raised to the head to draw the blessing of intellect. Through this he tears the arm and skull of the disputants and idolaters. Leah said: "bagad" [dealt treacherously] — Rashi: "when he came to my handmaid, it was like a man being unfaithful to the wife of his youth" — he descended to the Chambers of Exchange (= the handmaids). But Leah boasted in this, for through this comes the essential tikun. "Ba Gad" — good fortune has come! The essential blessing of mazal tov recited with joy at a birth is specifically through this — through sorting from the Chambers of Exchange.

Asher — "in my good fortune, for women have called me fortunate": the completeness of joy — "fortunate is the man" — with which David began Sefer Tehillim. The aspect of "fortunate are we — how good is our portion!" with which we boast daily. "Fortunate are you, Israel" — with which Moshe concluded his blessings for Asher (in Parshas V'Zos HaBerachah); all Moshe's blessings parallel Yaakov our father's blessings, as Rashi explains.

Then Reuven found the duda'im [mandrakes] in the field — the aspect of "the mandrakes give forth fragrance." Both mandrakes — the good and the bad — both gave forth fragrance, as our Sages say. This is the great power of the tzadikim who gladden all and transform sorrow and sighing to joy, through which comes the essential begetting. Rachel wanted them, and Leah said: "is it a small thing that you took my husband?" — she saw through ruach hakodesh that she still needed to beget holy offspring. Then Yissachar was born — the great Torah scholars, the essential joy: "the statutes of Hashem are upright, gladdening the heart" — the joy of the mitzvah. From the sons of Yissachar came those who understood the times — to intercalate years and fix the months: the essential tikun of the moon's blemish through joy. "To know what Israel should do" — they knew how to gladden each person, teaching him what to do at each time to be saved from the bitterness of exile (= sadness), and to merit the joy of Israel — the totality of holiness.

Zevulun — "rejoice, Zevulun, in your going out." Zevulun engaged in commerce to support his brother Yissachar the Torah scholar — the essential tikun of wealth and money, where the essential hold of sadness resides ("in sadness you shall eat it"). The tikun is through Zevulun supporting Yissachar: "rejoice, Zevulun."

Then: "G-d remembered Rachel" etc. Even though ten holy tribes had already been born who reveal His G-dliness to gladden in Him always — nevertheless, Yosef still needed to be born, through whom comes the essential inflaming of Israel's joy. He is "a man in whom the spirit of G-d resides" — fanning the dust from the Jewish heart each time. Therefore Hashem's mercy was aroused, and He remembered Rachel on Rosh HaShanah — Yosef the tzadik was born, through whom comes the completeness of joy.

Then immediately Yaakov said: "send me away" — so the bed would not be completed outside Eretz Yisrael, as above. He merited that Binyamin was born in Eretz Yisrael — the Bais HaMikdash in his portion. After the joy was completed through the birth of the tribes, the Place was still needed — to receive the light of this joy: the awesome Place of the Bais HaMikdash, the source of joy: "eternal joy upon their heads."

Rachel was remembered on Rosh HaShanah like Sarah our mother (who bore Yitzchak on Rosh HaShanah). On Rosh HaShanah the world was created — to reveal His G-dliness in the world, all the joy, the vitality and sustenance of the world: "Hashem shall rejoice in His works." Sarah was remembered and bore Yitzchak — the first holy birth, named for joy. But the essential begetting of the complete bed (= all Israel) was through Yaakov, who begot twelve tribes — the totality of joy: "let Israel rejoice in its Maker." The bed's completion was through Rachel, who bore Yosef and Binyamin — therefore she too was remembered on Rosh HaShanah, when the Creation must be rectified and Adam HaRishon's sin ("in sadness you shall eat it" — from which all sadness and exiles come) must be repaired. On Rosh HaShanah we engage in this tikun, reading the portion of Hashem remembering Sarah; and Rachel's remembrance (for through her bearing Yosef and Binyamin comes the completeness of joy that began with Yitzchak). On Rosh HaShanah we blow the shofar — encompassing all ten types of melody (= the totality of joy): "fortunate is the people that knows the teruah"; "in Your Name they shall exult all day"; "the joy of Hashem is your strength," said regarding Rosh HaShanah. Chanah too was remembered on Rosh HaShanah, bearing Shmuel the prophet — who anointed Shaul and David: the tikun of Malchus, from which Mashiach will emerge to redeem Israel, when all joy will be complete, speedily in our days, amain.

This is the aspect of Menasheh and Efrayim. Menasheh — "G-d has made me forget all my toil": the toil, sorrow, etc. Efrayim — "G-d has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction": not only was he saved from the slavery (= sadness, toil, and sorrow), and in His kindness "made me forget all my toil" — He even "made me fruitful in the land of my affliction": the transformation of poverty and sadness to joy.

§ 57 — "These Are the Names of the Children of Israel Coming to Egypt": Survival Through Joy

"These are the names of the children of Israel coming to Egypt, with Yaakov" etc. When the Torah begins telling of the Egyptian exile and redemption, it starts with the names of the children of Israel who came there — to show that all their survival in exile and their redemption derived from the power of the names of the children of Israel: Reuven, Shimon, Levi, etc. — all named for the joy of Israel. Through this they sorted from the Chambers of Exchange, perceiving the Ain Sof light — the essential purpose of the ge'ulah: "you shall know that I am Hashem who brings you out."

Hashem arranged that Yaakov and his righteous sons would descend to Egypt first, for through their awesome holiness (the complete bed revealing His G-dliness in the world = the essential joy and vitality), they had the strength to bear the exile's bitterness without being swallowed up there. The essential bitterness of exile is sadness. The more exile is intensified, the more sadness overpowers — and the more sadness overpowers (= the exile of the Shechinah), the more physical exile and slavery intensify. From where then shall our help come? All survival in exile and hope of leaving comes through the tzadikim — Yaakov and his sons who descended to Egypt — the above-named children of Israel. Through their great power and deep counsel, they can draw His G-dliness, reviving and gladdening every Jewish soul, raising Malchus each time through all the ascents until the ge'ulah: "for with joy you shall go out."

"Yosef was in Egypt" — the essential survival and hope is through Yosef the tzadik, "a man in whom there is spirit" — who knows each time to fan the dust (= sadness) from the Jewish heart and inflame it for Hashem in gradation and measure. He knows how to transform all sorrow and sighing to gladness and joy. "All who emerged from Yaakov's thigh were seventy souls" — the seventy faces of the Torah, the seventy shining countenances (= joy): "those who seek Your face — Yaakov" etc. (as explained in the Torah "Tzavisa Tzedek"). "Yosef was in Egypt" — the essential thing through Yosef, whom Hashem sent ahead as a remedy before the affliction. He was sold as a slave (= the bitterness of sadness = slavery), yet he stood the test and strengthened himself even there with joy, as it says: "Yosef was a successful man" — the Midrash explains: leaping and dancing. In the bitterness of exile when sadness intensifies, the essential counsel is to do foolish things to gladden one's soul in such bitterness.

segments.he: וזהו בחינת חצות. כי הלילה נחלקת לשתים כי היא בבחינת עץ הדעת טוב ורע. ועל כן נחלקת לשתים, כי חצות לילה הראשונה אז הוא בחינת אחיזת הסטרא אחרא כמובא . ואנחנו עושין מצוות ותקונים גם בחצי לילה הראשונה דהינו תפלת ערבית וקריאת שמע, וקריאת שמע שעל המטה. ואז מכניעין הרע ומבררין הטוב, ואז זוכין לחצות דהינו לחלק את הלילה שיתהפך חצות לילה האחרונה לטוב גמור, ולהכלל ביום, ולילה כיום יאיר (תהלים קלט). כי מחצות ואילך מתגלה בחינת חסד שהוא אור היום. ועל כן דוד המלך עליו השלום היה נזהר בחצות. כי זהו שלמות המלכות שהוא בחינת שלמות לשון הקדש על ידי תרגום, שהוא בחינת חצות כנזכר לעיל. ועל כן זמן הזווג אחר חצות. כי אז נבנה בחינת חוה אשה על ידי תקון עץ הדעת. שהוא בחינת תרדמה ושנה שנעשה על ידי חצות שהוא שבירת השנה שבירת הלילה. בחינת שבירת עץ הדעת. ואזי נכלל בטוב, ולילה כיום יאיר. ועל כן מחצות מתגלה חסד אור היום כנזכר לעיל:
segments.en:
As it says of David: he changed his behavior before Avimelech — being in great danger in a great exile, he did seemingly foolish acts: "he scribbled on the doors of the gate and let his saliva run down his beard" etc. Therefore, their essential survival in Egypt and their exodus was through "Yosef was in Egypt" — Hashem sent the tzadik ahead, as above.

"They embittered their lives with hard labor, with mortar and bricks" etc. The essential bitterness of exile is slavery — drawn from the contamination of the serpent: "in sadness you shall eat it" — the overpowering of sadness. This is the miry clay David cried about: "I sank in deep mire, with no foothold... save me from the mire." The holy Zohar explains: "with hard labor" = with difficult questions; "with mortar" = with the severity of Talmudic argumentation; "and with bricks" = with the clarification of halachah. The essential bitterness of exile confuses the joy in Him (= holy emunah, shining countenances) through the difficulties and confusions — the severity of argumentation and clarification of halachah. The essential "raising a teaching to the level of halachah" is to clarify and whiten true counsel for serving the Creator — to leave the contamination of this lowly world and draw close to Hashem, for "not study but practice is the essential thing." This is why the essential drawing close to Torah scholars and true tzadikim is so important — so they can teach us the way to walk and the deed to do at each time, so each person merits leaving what he must leave and returning to Hashem.

But the Sitra Achra — the bitterness of exile (= sadness) — overpowers greatly, embittering Israel's lives with difficulties and confusions of emunah and confusions of counsel, until people do not know how to whiten the halachah — the path and way to return to Hashem. "With all labor in the field" — the craving for money and the burden of livelihood, compelled to leave the tent of Torah and go to the field to engage in livelihood, until one is so burdened with all field-labor and enticed away from even setting fixed times for Torah study.

"All their labor was with parech" — our Sages expound: b'feh rach [with a soft mouth]. At first the ba'al davar and Sitra Achra enter with a soft mouth, clothing themselves in mitzvos, saying: "It's impossible to sit in the bais midrash all day; you must go to the field to work and do business. Do you want to die or be a pauper?" etc. — until they cast him into the deep miry clay: the dark countenances of sadness over money ("in sadness you shall eat it"). Even when he earns, it never suffices — he always craves more: "the more possessions, the more worry" — "it was not known they had come." They entice him to build Pisom and Ramses — great, tall buildings for themselves: "they call their houses by their names forever" etc.

§ 58 — Pharaoh's Decree: "Every Son Born — Cast into the River"

This is Pharaoh's decree: "every son that is born..." etc.; "if it is a son, kill him; if a daughter, she shall live." A son — the male side (= joy): "a wise son gladdens a father." A daughter — the female side, where the essential hold of sadness resides: "her feet descend to death." Pharaoh wanted to strengthen the female side (= sadness) — the essential force of exile.

"The midwives feared G-d and did not do as Pharaoh commanded; they kept the children alive." The midwives are the tzadikim of the generation — who give birth, raising worthy students in Israel (considered as if they birthed them, as our Sages say). They acted opposite to the Sitra Achra (= Pharaoh and Egypt, whose entire agenda is to strengthen sadness through many stratagems — primarily through the burden of money and livelihood, and sometimes through the reversed reasoning from the Chambers of Exchange that cast a person down through improper rebuke, etc.). But the above midwives (= the true tzadikim) do the opposite: not only do they not cast people down with their words as the Sitra Achra desires, but "they kept the children alive" — reviving their students and those attached to them through their true words, restoring their souls through comforting counsel, gladdening them through their power and deep counsel, as above.

Therefore the midwives were named Shifrah and Pu'ah: Shifrah — she beautifies the infant; Pu'ah — she cries out to the infant, etc., as our Sages say. This is how the true tzadikim conduct themselves with the Jewish souls attached to them: they beautify them and make them lovely through all kinds of counsel to revive and strengthen them in every good point found in them, etc. And they cry out to them like to an actual infant — whistling and calling to them not to let themselves fall in any way, but to trust in Hashem's kindnesses that are never exhausted, and in the great power of the tzadikim who will never abandon them: "not according to our sins does He deal with us"; there is always hope (as explained extensively in the holy sefarim, especially in our writings; see there well).

§ 59 — The Burning Bush: The Fire of Joy Amidst the Thorns of Exile

This is the aspect of the vision of the Sneh [bush] and why Moshe refused his mission for so long. Essentially, he saw through ruach hakodesh the length of the bitter present exile — impossible to fathom its end, for it is the wondrous end. Therefore he did not want to go on his mission, as our Sages say (explained in Rashi on "send, please, by the hand You will send"): "I know I will not bring them into Eretz Yisrael and will not redeem them in the future," etc. — all because of the great dispute among Israel, until they do not know where the true tzadikim are — the essential prolonging of exile, as is known.

"He saw, and behold, the bush burned with fire, yet the bush was not consumed." He was greatly astonished: why is the bush not consumed? The bush alludes to the exile, as our Sages say. He saw the revelation of G-dliness in a flame of fire from within the bush — the inflaming of the Jewish heart burning for Hashem through the power of the true tzadikim ("a man in whom there is spirit") — burning for Hashem from within the bush, from within the bitterness of exile. Yet "the bush was not consumed" — the exile still overpowers, the bitterness of sadness ("the bush was not consumed": the thorns and briers surrounding the rose, whose essence is sadness = the exile of the Shechinah) is not consumed, overpowering each time.

Moshe was greatly astonished and said: "let me turn aside and see this great sight — why the bush is not consumed." He wanted to reach the very end — how Israel will merit the complete ge'ulah with no exile after it, consuming the bush (= the thorns and briers) completely. Then: "Hashem saw that he turned aside to look, and called to him... 'Do not come closer... remove your shoes from your feet, for the place upon which you stand is holy ground.'" This is the obstructer — the Arranger and Settler who prevents the pursuing mind from breaking through to Hashem, as above.

Moshe, the first righteous redeemer, saw he would redeem Israel — he could gladden Israel amidst the exile's bitterness, illuminating within them the sparkling of His G-dliness (= the essential joy): a flame of fire, "its sparks are sparks of fire, a flame of G-d" — revealed from within the bush, from within the exile's bitterness, for he could transform sorrow and sighing to joy. Yet "the bush was not consumed" — they overpower each time with many stratagems without limit. They caused Israel to sin greatly immediately after the giving of the Torah, etc. — the ten trials, etc. — through which all the exiles were decreed until this long, bitter exile. As it says: "on the day I make account..." etc.

Moshe wanted to fathom this — the perception of the wondrous end. Hashem said: "do not come closer" — the obstructer, the Arranger and Settler. For Moshe then merited the perception of the above nine chambers through the joy of the mitzvah (= the sparkling of receiving the Torah that began then), perceiving and seeing what he perceived. But he saw the bush was still not consumed and said: "let me turn aside and see" — how to perceive G-dliness with such joy as to consume the bush completely. As explained above: one depends on the other — the more one overpowers with the joy of the mitzvah, the more one merits some sprouting of salvation, raising the Shechinah from exile and ascending through all the above ascents until the nine chambers where the source of joy resides ("eternal joy upon their heads"). Then one draws additional joy from the source, and then one can sort even more from the Chambers of Exchange — and then ascend even higher to the nine chambers in greater perception, and joy grows even more, and one can sort even more — and so on. If this had proceeded in order, certainly the end of the ge'ulah (through joy) would have arrived. But our sins have caused this — each time the ba'al davar overpowers, causing Israel to sin and strengthening sadness: "they provoked Him in the wilderness" — confusions of emunah (= idolatry and heresy, called atzabim [idols] for sadness [atzvus]: "their idols are silver and gold").

Through this the exile is prolonged — "Israel was exiled only because faithful people ceased among them" etc. (= sadness itself). But the great tzadikim of every generation labor with their great power to gladden Israel through illuminating holy emunah in their hearts each time. But the essential prolonging of exile is through the dispute that strives to distance Jewish hearts from the true tzadikim. Through this, the ultimate end cannot be fathomed — even Moshe Rabbainu could not, for Hashem told him: "do not come closer" — the Chambers of Exchange have not yet been sufficiently sorted for you to ascend and perceive further. All perception of the Ain Sof light depends on the sorting from the Chambers of Exchange through mi yaimar.

"Remove your shoes from your feet, for the place upon which you stand is holy ground" — to here extends the holiness of the above supernal Place (= the obstructer, "blessed is the glory of Hashem from His place"). One needs the removal of shoes — stripping oneself completely from the body of this world, as stated in the holy Zohar. But to go further — to perceive how to consume the bush completely — is impossible now. This too is the aspect of the waiting: one must wait a great deal until we merit such sorting from the Chambers of Exchange that the tzadikim will perceive how to consume the bush completely.

Therefore Moshe indeed refused his mission for seven days, saying: "send by the hand You will send," as above.

§ 60 — Aharon's Joy: "He Saw You and Rejoiced in His Heart" — The Root of the Ge'ulah

Until finally: "Hashem's anger burned against Moshe, and He said: 'Is not Aharon your brother the Levi?... He is coming out to meet you, and when he sees you, he will rejoice in his heart.'" "He will rejoice in his heart" specifically — through this comes the essential tikun of the ge'ulah: through the great peace he would have with Moshe, not being jealous at all. On the contrary — rejoicing in his heart. The essential tikun is through joy — raising Malchus from the Chambers of Exchange, etc. — meriting the above blessings: the holiness of the priesthood ("Aharon raised his hands and blessed"). Therefore Aharon merited the holiness of the priesthood through "he will rejoice in his heart," as our Sages say.

Through this came the Egyptian redemption — for the essential ge'ulah is through joy, and the essential completeness of joy is through peace: "for with joy you shall go out and in peace be led." Hashem revealed to Moshe that he must go on his mission to redeem Israel and give us the Torah — without him, Israel would never be redeemed, as the Midrash states: "if you do not redeem them, no one else will." Specifically because of the length of the present exile — he must go and give the Torah. Had we not received the Torah through Moshe Rabbainu, survival in this long, bitter exile would be impossible. As the holy Zohar states: our essential hope now is that Hashem already provided the remedy before the affliction — we already received the Torah and mitzvos through Moshe. Through this we can gladden ourselves each time through the abundance of mitzvos we merit performing daily (even the simplest person) — essentially through the great tzadikim of each generation who instill in us the joy of the mitzvah-points, etc. — raising the Shechinah each time until the complete ge'ulah.

Without the Torah, it would be impossible to gladden our souls now or leave the exile. In Egypt, where the exile of Edom had not yet intensified, the holiness of Yaakov and his sons (especially Yosef the tzadik) sufficed to sustain and survive the exile. But now, in the crushing pressure of the final exile, survival without the Torah and mitzvos (which are our life and joy: "we shall rejoice in the words of Your Torah and Your mitzvos forever, for they are our life"; "were Your Torah not my delight, I would have perished in my affliction") would be impossible.

But the essential power of the Egyptian ge'ulah then was through "he saw you and rejoiced in his heart" — Aharon, who merited the holiness of the priesthood through this (the blessing of the hands, etc. — through which the nine chambers are perceived, from which all perception of G-dliness derives — the essential purpose of the ge'ulah). The essential delay of the ge'ulah then was through Dasan and Aviram — the heads of the disputants and their followers, from whom all corruptions and trials came, leading to all the destructions (the first and second Bais HaMikdash, all the sufferings, Rachmana litzlan, up to this final exile whose essential prolonging is through dispute, as above). In every dispute there are sparks of Dasan and Aviram, as our Sages say.

Nevertheless: "You are eternally exalted, Hashem." Then Aharon the Kohain was found — not jealous of the greatness of Moshe his younger brother. On the contrary: he went out to meet him with joy — through which came the first ge'ulah, and the holiness of the priesthood was drawn. Through the power of Moshe and Aharon the Kohain, there are found now, in every generation, true tzadikim and upright people who attach themselves to the great chosen tzadikim, rejoicing to meet them, heeding their counsel, gladdening their souls in performing every mitzvah. Through this will come the complete ge'ulah: "for with joy you shall go out and in peace be led," as above.

§ 61 — Birchas SheHechiyanu [The Blessing of Who Has Kept Us Alive]: The Joy of Seeing a Beloved Fellow Jew

This is the aspect of Birchas SheHechiyanu [the Blessing of Who Has Kept Us Alive]: when one sees a friend who is dear to him and rejoices at seeing him, he blesses SheHechiyanu [Who Has Kept Us Alive]. This is the essential vitality and sustenance — when one rejoices at seeing a fellow Jew. The essential joy is that two Jews who love each other merited meeting together in peace — through which the joy of Israel is greatly increased. Every Jew has a portion of G-dliness from above — the source of joy: "let Israel rejoice in its Maker." But the klipah that precedes the fruit (= sadness) covers over it, and a great struggle is needed to overpower joy over sadness — a great battle. Therefore, many Jewish souls must join and gather together. The more souls join in love, the more joy increases — the portions of joy are gathered and joined, shining with even greater light: "the light of the righteous makes glad" (ois mem-bais above); "when the righteous multiply, the people rejoice."

Therefore, upon seeing a beloved fellow Jew, we bless: SheHechiyanu v'kiy'manu [Who has kept us alive and sustained us] — for this is the essential vitality and sustenance [hechyah and kiyum], through joy and peace. This is "he saw you and rejoiced in his heart" — through which came the essential Egyptian ge'ulah: Aharon was not jealous of his younger brother Moshe's greatness. The essential ge'ulah is through joy — essentially through the love of friends who strive to draw close to Hashem in truth: "he saw you and rejoiced in his heart."
